You don't want the user to be anxious.

## Update — review and hardening

The change has been reviewed and improved with AI assistance, and validated on real hardware.

### Why this is not a duplicate
This updates the existing PR (the only open one for prefill progress reporting). No other open PR addresses `return_progress` / `prompt_progress`:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prompt_progress in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "return_progress"
```

### What changed since the first review
- **Opt-in on the engine hot path.** The scheduler now emits a partial-prefill
  `EngineCoreOutput` only when the request set `return_progress` (plumbed via
  `SamplingParams`); `num_computed_tokens` is carried only for those requests.
  Before, an output was produced on every prefill chunk for *all* requests,
  adding work even when no client asked for progress.
- **Cache disclosure gated.** The `cache` field (`num_cached_tokens`) is now
  gated behind the server-side `enable_prompt_tokens_details` flag, matching
  every other cached-token disclosure in the serving layer.
- **Typed response model** `PromptProgress` instead of a raw `dict[str, int]`.
- Removed the redundant `num_computed_tokens < num_tokens` scheduler condition
  (subsumed by `is_prefill_chunk`), fixed the now-nuanced invariant comment,
  made the completion `total` consistent (incl. encoder tokens), and cleaned up
  formatting/lint.

### Tests run and results
- Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all touched files.
- New tests: `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_progress.py`.
- Live validation on an RTX 5090 (real server, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`,
  `--enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --enable-prefix-caching`):
  - chat & completion: `prompt_progress` is emitted with `return_progress=true`
    (`processed` advances by the chunk size, e.g. `512, 768, … 1792`, `total=2009`),
    and is **absent by default** (no extra prefill outputs);
  - `cache = 0` without `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, and disclosed
    (e.g. `320`) with it.

### AI assistance disclosure
AI assistance (Claude) was used to review the original change and to implement
these improvements and tests. The change was reviewed by a human submitter.

Heads-up for getting this onto current main: the diff no longer applies to the 0.30.x tree (12+ failing hunks across 8 files). The two blockers we hit when porting it:

1. `vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py` no longer exists after the entrypoints reorg — `PromptProgress` now belongs in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/engine/protocol.py`.
2. The v1 scheduler now gates prefill output emission through the pre-computed `should_emit_output` flag, so the `return_progress` condition needs to fold into that flag rather than the inline emit-site check.

We're running a hand-port of this on 0.30.0 in production (opt-in `return_progress` drives a client-side prefill progress bar) and it behaves as specified. For reference, the port is at syv-ai/HyperQwen#296.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `return_progress` feature for OpenAI-compatible chat and completion endpoints, enabling clients to receive streaming updates on prefill progress via a new `prompt_progress` field. The implementation involves updating protocol schemas, propagating `num_computed_tokens` through the V1 engine and scheduler, and adjusting metrics to account for prefill chunks. Review feedback identifies a precision issue in the `time_ms` calculation within the serving logic, where using integer-truncated timestamps for millisecond-level reporting can result in significant inaccuracies.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The calculation of `time_ms` can be inaccurate by up to 1 second when `res.metrics.arrival_time` is not available. This is because `created_time` is an integer timestamp, created by `int(time.time())`, which truncates sub-second precision. For a feature reporting progress in milliseconds, this level of inaccuracy is significant and can lead to misleading metrics.

To fix this, a floating-point timestamp should be captured at the start of the request and used for this duration calculation.

Additionally, the current implementation calls `time.time()` twice, which is inefficient and can introduce minor inconsistencies.

Here's a suggested refactoring of this block. Please note that a complete fix also requires changing how `created_time` is initialized at the beginning of this function to preserve float precision for time calculations.

```suggestion
                    now = time.time()
                    start_time = res.metrics.arrival_time if res.metrics and hasattr(res.metrics, "arrival_time") else created_time
                    time_ms = int((now - start_time) * 1000)
```

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the streaming ``return_progress`` / ``prompt_progress`` feature.
+
+The feature reports prefill progress on the OpenAI-compatible streaming
+endpoints. It is opt-in per request (``return_progress=True``) and must be
+invisible to every other request, including on the engine hot path.
+"""
+
+import json
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+
+from ...utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+
+# Any small model with a chat template works here.
+MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
+
+# Long prompt so that, with a small ``--max-num-batched-tokens``, prefill is
+# split into several chunks and therefore reports progress more than once.
+LONG_PROMPT = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 200
+
+# A cacheable prefix followed by a long uncached tail. Priming with the prefix
+# then sending ``CACHE_PREFIX + CACHE_TAIL`` yields a request whose prefill both
+# hits the prefix cache (``cache > 0``) and still chunks over the tail (so at
+# least one progress chunk is emitted while the cache hit is visible).
+CACHE_PREFIX = "Background. " + ("vLLM serves large language models. " * 40)
+CACHE_TAIL = "Now continue the detailed analysis. " * 200
+
+_PROGRESS_KEYS = {"total", "cache", "processed", "time_ms"}
+
+BASE_ARGS = [
+    "--dtype",
+    "bfloat16",
+    "--max-model-len",
+    "8192",
+    "--enforce-eager",
+    "--max-num-seqs",
+    "8",
+    "--enable-chunked-prefill",
+    "--max-num-batched-tokens",
+    "256",
+    "--enable-prefix-caching",
+    # The cache-disclosure test keeps two servers alive on the same GPU.
+    "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+    "0.4",
+]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server():
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(MODEL_NAME, BASE_ARGS) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server_with_token_details():
+    # ``--enable-prompt-tokens-details`` is the server-side gate that allows
+    # disclosing cached-token counts.
+    args = BASE_ARGS + ["--enable-prompt-tokens-details"]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(MODEL_NAME, args) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+async def _collect_sse(
+    server: RemoteOpenAIServer, path: tuple[str, ...], payload: dict
+) -> list[dict]:
+    """Stream a raw SSE response and return the parsed ``data:`` chunks.
+
+    The raw stream is used (rather than the typed OpenAI client) so that the
+    non-standard top-level ``prompt_progress`` field is preserved as-is.
+    """
+    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {server.DUMMY_API_KEY}"}
+    chunks: list[dict] = []
+    async with (
+        httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120.0) as client,
+        client.stream(
+            "POST", server.url_for(*path), json=payload, headers=headers
+        ) as response,
+    ):
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        async for line in response.aiter_lines():
+            if not line.startswith("data: "):
+                continue
+            data = line[len("data: ") :]
+            if data.strip() == "[DONE]":
+                break
+            chunks.append(json.loads(data))
+    return chunks
+
+
+def _progress_reports(chunks: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
+    return [
+        c["prompt_progress"] for c in chunks if c.get("prompt_progress") is not None
+    ]
+
+
+def _assert_progress_shape(reports: list[dict], *, expect_cache_hidden: bool) -> None:
+    assert reports, "expected at least one prompt_progress chunk"
+    total = reports[0]["total"]
+    last_processed = -1
+    for report in reports:
+        assert set(report) == _PROGRESS_KEYS
+        assert all(isinstance(value, int) for value in report.values())
+        assert report["total"] == total > 0
+        assert 0 <= report["processed"] <= total
+        # ``processed`` advances monotonically across prefill chunks.
+        assert report["processed"] >= last_processed
+        last_processed = report["processed"]
+        assert report["time_ms"] >= 0
+        if expect_cache_hidden:
+            assert report["cache"] == 0
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_chat_progress_streaming(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    payload = {
+        "model": MODEL_NAME,
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": LONG_PROMPT}],
+        "max_tokens": 5,
+        "temperature": 0.0,
+        "stream": True,
+        "return_progress": True,
+    }
+    chunks = await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "chat", "completions"), payload)
+    reports = _progress_reports(chunks)
+    _assert_progress_shape(reports, expect_cache_hidden=True)
+    # Progress chunks must carry no choices.
+    for chunk in chunks:
+        if chunk.get("prompt_progress") is not None:
+            assert chunk["choices"] == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_completion_progress_streaming(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    payload = {
+        "model": MODEL_NAME,
+        "prompt": LONG_PROMPT,
+        "max_tokens": 5,
+        "temperature": 0.0,
+        "stream": True,
+        "return_progress": True,
+    }
+    chunks = await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "completions"), payload)
+    reports = _progress_reports(chunks)
+    _assert_progress_shape(reports, expect_cache_hidden=True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_chat_no_progress_by_default(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    # Regression guard for the engine-side opt-in gate: without return_progress
+    # the scheduler must not emit partial-prefill outputs, so no prompt_progress
+    # chunk may appear.
+    payload = {
+        "model": MODEL_NAME,
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": LONG_PROMPT}],
+        "max_tokens": 5,
+        "temperature": 0.0,
+        "stream": True,
+    }
+    chunks = await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "chat", "completions"), payload)
+    assert _progress_reports(chunks) == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_completion_no_progress_by_default(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    payload = {
+        "model": MODEL_NAME,
+        "prompt": LONG_PROMPT,
+        "max_tokens": 5,
+        "temperature": 0.0,
+        "stream": True,
+    }
+    chunks = await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "completions"), payload)
+    assert _progress_reports(chunks) == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_cache_field_respects_enable_prompt_tokens_details(
+    server: RemoteOpenAIServer,
+    server_with_token_details: RemoteOpenAIServer,
+):
+    def payload(prompt: str) -> dict:
+        return {
+            "model": MODEL_NAME,
+            "prompt": prompt,
+            "max_tokens": 5,
+            "temperature": 0.0,
+            "stream": True,
+            "return_progress": True,
+        }
+
+    hit_prompt = CACHE_PREFIX + CACHE_TAIL
+
+    # Default server: cached tokens must stay hidden (0) even on a cache hit.
+    await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "completions"), payload(CACHE_PREFIX))
+    chunks = await _collect_sse(server, ("v1", "completions"), payload(hit_prompt))
+    default_reports = _progress_reports(chunks)
+    assert default_reports
+    assert all(report["cache"] == 0 for report in default_reports)
+
+    # With --enable-prompt-tokens-details the cache hit may be disclosed.
+    await _collect_sse(

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The calculation of `time_ms` can be inaccurate by up to 1 second when `res.metrics.arrival_time` is not available. This is because `created_time` is an integer timestamp, created by `int(time.time())`, which truncates sub-second precision. For a feature reporting progress in milliseconds, this level of inaccuracy is significant and can lead to misleading metrics.

To fix this, a floating-point timestamp should be captured at the start of the request and used for this duration calculation.

Additionally, the current implementation calls `time.time()` twice, which is inefficient and can introduce minor inconsistencies.

Here's a suggested refactoring of this block. Please note that a complete fix also requires changing how `created_time` is initialized at the beginning of this function to preserve float precision for time calculations.

```suggestion
                    now = time.time()
                    start_time = res.metrics.arrival_time if res.metrics and hasattr(res.metrics, "arrival_time") else created_time
                    time_ms = int((now - start_time) * 1000)
```

Heads-up for getting this onto current main: the diff no longer applies to the 0.30.x tree (12+ failing hunks across 8 files). The two blockers we hit when porting it:

1. `vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py` no longer exists after the entrypoints reorg — `PromptProgress` now belongs in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/engine/protocol.py`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a `return_progress` feature for OpenAI-compatible chat and completion endpoints, enabling clients to receive streaming updates on prefill progress via a new `prompt_progress` field. The implementation involves updating protocol schemas, propagating `num_computed_tokens` through the V1 engine and scheduler, and adjusting metrics to account for prefill chunks. Review feedback identifies a precision issue in the `time_ms` calculation within the serving logic, where using integer-truncated timestamps for millisecond-level reporting can result in significant inaccuracies.
